name: LT1028 / LT1128 (single ultralow-noise bipolar, 0.85 nV/√Hz)
tagline: A 0.85 nV/√Hz bipolar single from Linear Tech. It has long been the benchmark for MC, tape-head and mic head-amps, and it is a cult pick for op-amp rolling (e.g., Xonar I/V stages).
technology: Bipolar single op amp. The input stage runs at nearly 1 mA collector current, so voltage noise is very low but current noise is high. Bias-current cancellation holds IB to about 25 nA typ; the cancellation injects correlated current noise, which is rejected only when the source resistances are matched. The LT1028 is decompensated: stable at gain >= +2 or -1, 75 MHz GBW. The LT1128 is the unity-gain-stable version, 20 MHz GBW. Pin 5 is an over-compensation terminal and pins 1/8 are VOS trim. The inputs have back-to-back protection diodes with no series resistors.

lineage.period: by 1989 (a TI-library macromodel is dated 08/31/89) until the 2017 ADI acquisition. The combined LT1028/LT1128 datasheet carries (c) 1992; Revs B (10/12), C (10/14) and D (10/15) were issued under Linear.
lineage.notes: The datasheet code is '1028f' plus a revision letter (1028fd = Rev D; a Scribd copy titled '1028fc' is Rev C). The Rev D page header reads 'For more information www.linear.com/LT1028'. Introduction date and designer not verified.

TI's op-amp macromodel library (TEXAS.LIB) contains an 'LT1028 operational amplifier macromodel' created 08/31/89, next to TI-made models for LT1013 and LT1037, which TI is known to have second-sourced. A targeted 2026 web search found no TI LT1028 datasheet or SLOS number. Low confidence.

ADI hosts the Linear-branded 1028fd.pdf (Rev D) and live LT1028 and LT1128 product pages (both web-confirmed). A web search for a newer revision ('Rev E' / '1028fe') returned only 1028fd. No PCN or die change was found. The LTspice changelog shows LT1028 model and symbol fixes in 2023.

key_specs.source: LT1028/LT1128 datasheet 1028fd Rev D, p.3 (0.85 nV/rtHz headline web-confirmed)

key_specs.condition: +/-15 V, 25 C. 10 Hz density is lot-sample-tested except S8/S16; 0.1-10 Hz is sample-tested only.

key_specs.value: 1.0 pA/rtHz typ @ 1 kHz (1.6 max A, 1.8 max non-A); 4.7 pA/rtHz typ @ 10 Hz (10.0 max A, 12.0 max non-A). Current-noise 1/f corner typically 250 Hz.

key_specs.source: 1028fd Rev D, p.3 (page-1 minimums of 11 V/us / 5 V/us web-confirmed)

key_specs.value: Not tabulated; graphs only. THD vs frequency at AV = +/-1000, VO = 20 Vp-p, RL = 600 ohm / 2 kohm. THD vs closed-loop gain at 1 kHz, RL = 10 kohm (measured plus extrapolated). The sine-oscillator application circuit claims '<0.0018% distortion and noise', limited by the HP339A analyzer's resolution.
PSRR specified for +/-4 V to +/-18 V (25 C). Absolute max +/-22 V (-55 to 105 C) and +/-16 V (105 to 125 C). AC/C operating range -40 to 85 C (not tested at the extremes); specified 0 to 70 C.
7.4 mA typ, 9.5 max (A); 7.6 typ, 10.5 max (non-A) at 25 C. Over 0-70 C: 10.5 max (A) / 11.5 max (non-A). Over -40 to 85 C: 11.0 (A) / 12.5 (non-A) max.
+/-12.2 V typ into 600 ohm (+/-11.0 min A). +/-13.0 V typ into 2 kohm. Open-loop Zo 80 ohm. Short-circuit duration indefinite; short-circuit current is only graphed.

VOS 10 uV typ, 40 max (A); 20 uV typ, 80 max (non-A). Drift 0.1 uV/C typ, 0.8 max (A) / 0.2 typ, 1.0 max (non-A) over 0-70 C. IB +/-25 nA typ, +/-90 max (A). AVOL 30 V/uV typ, 7.0 min (A) at RL >= 2k. CMRR 126 dB typ.

Bipolar, nearly 1 mA collector current. Back-to-back input diodes with no limiting resistors: limit current to 25 mA if the differential input exceeds +/-1.8 V. The optimum source resistance is about e_n/i_n = 850 ohm at 1 kHz (computed from typ values). Datasheet Table 1 names the LT1028/LT1128 as LT's lowest-noise choice for 0-400 ohm sources at 10 Hz and up to 4 kohm at 1 kHz. Because of bias-current cancellation, unmatched source resistance above about 1 kohm adds cancellation noise.

The LT1028 is stable at closed-loop gain > +2 or -1 (about 50 deg phase margin at 6 dB). As a follower it needs parallel RC feedback (CF < 68 pF) or source resistance. A large CF can oscillate unless RS2 >= 500 ohm. The LT1128 is unity-gain stable. A capacitor from pin 5 (over-comp) to the output cuts noise bandwidth and improves capacitive-load drive.

Rev C (10/14) corrected the right-hand (non-A-grade) Electrical Characteristics column and changed TJMAX to 150 C for S8/SW. Non-A limits printed in Rev B or earlier copies (including third-party mirrors that freeze older sheets) may therefore be wrong.

reputation.summary: Hi-Fi enthusiasts and engineers treat the LT1028 as the reference ultralow-noise bipolar op amp for very low source impedances: MC phono head amps, tape heads and dynamic mics. Its own datasheet shows MAG phono and tape-head preamps. In diyAudio's 'The best sounding audio integrated opamps' thread, one poster calls it 'the only real L.T. star' (web-confirmed). Several diyAudio threads build MC/MM RIAA stages around it, and an Audio Asylum thread weighs it against the AD797 for MC phono. It is sold as a single DIP-8 for op-amp rolling (e.g., Audiophonics) and is a popular I/V pick for Asus Xonar Essence ST/STX rolling. Japanese Dr.DAC users call it monitor-like and not fussy about sources, and Aurorasound presented NS's LME49990 as a challenger to the LT1028A (both not re-verified). The 1993 rec.audio Audio FAQ already called it 'very well received' for phono, head-amp and mic preamps. Engineers note its high current noise and a noise bump around 400 kHz. The sonic descriptors are community opinion and were not re-verified.
typical_uses: MM phono and tape-head preamps (datasheet application circuits; diyAudio RIAA builds)
DAC I/V stage (e.g., Asus Xonar Essence ST/STX op-amp rolling)
op-amp rolling in Dr.DAC-type DACs and headphone amps
low-noise measurement preamps, TIAs, laser current drivers
caveats: The LT1028 is NOT unity-gain stable (gain >= +2 or -1). It can oscillate as a follower, unity buffer or I/V stage with a large feedback cap. Use the LT1128 or follow the datasheet RC/RS2 rules. With 75 MHz GBW it is sensitive to socket and adapter layout.

High input bias current (+/-25 nA) and current noise (1 pA/rtHz at 1 kHz, 4.7 at 10 Hz). With source impedances well above about 1 kohm (about 400 ohm at 10 Hz per the datasheet table), current noise dominates and another part is better. Bias-current cancellation adds noise when the source resistances at the two inputs are unmatched.

High supply current: 7.4 mA typ, 9.5-10.5 mA max at 25 C, and up to 12.5 mA max (non-A, -40 to 85 C). It runs warm and loads small supplies. It is specified at +/-15 V, and PSRR is specified from +/-4 V.
Single only, with no dual version. Dual sockets need adapters, which adds oscillation risk.
Pin 5 is an over-compensation pin and pins 1/8 are VOS trim. Check that the host board leaves pin 5 open or uses it correctly. The SW16 package has a different pinout and is NRND.
Input diodes have no series resistors. Large differential transients (for example slew overload in unity-gain use) need input current limiting.
There is a noise bump around 400 kHz in the HF noise curve. It is inaudible but raises integrated wideband noise (Libbrecht & Hall 1993 and Seck et al. 2016, as cited in P. Baus's PhD thesis).

'Replaced the Typical Application' (p.1). The page-1 circuit in Rev D is an ultralow-noise 1M TIA photodiode amplifier with an NXP BF862 JFET. Revs C and D list no page-1 change, so this is inferred to be the Rev B replacement.

counterfeit_notes:
No specific counterfeit reports were found; a web search found none. Marketplace listings exist, such as eBay lots of '1PCS LT1028ACN8 DIP-8 ... NEW' and '50 Stück ... LT1028CN8 ... NEU'. Their provenance is unknown, and a bulk lot of a part that sells for several dollars is a red flag. Identification per Rev D:
- SO-8 parts are top-marked '1028' / '1128' (plus date and lot code).
- PDIP and SW16 parts carry the full part number (e.g., 'LT1028ACN8').
- The temperature grade appears on the shipping-container label.
- #PBF / #TRPBF / #TRMPBF are orderable suffixes, not package markings.
- AM/M grades and the H (TO-5) and J8 (CERDIP) packages are obsolete, so 'new' metal-can or ceramic parts are old stock or fakes.
Quick bench checks at +/-15 V:
- A genuine part draws about 7.4 mA (9.5 mA max A grade, 10.5 mA non-A, at 25 C).
- Its 1 kHz noise should be at or below 1.1-1.2 nV/rtHz.
- A remarked generic bipolar op amp would typically show about 3 nV/rtHz or more.
- An LT1028 sold as a unity-gain buffer that proves stable at unity gain may be a relabelled LT1128 or another part.
alternatives: AD797 (ADI): about 0.9 nV/rtHz bipolar single with high output drive and a very low-distortion reputation. It is the usual head-to-head rival for MC phono (e.g., Audio Asylum 'LT1028 or AD797 for MC phono stage'). Seck et al. (via Baus) found lower integrated wideband noise than the LT1028, which has a 400 kHz bump.
LT1115 (Linear/ADI): 0.9 nV/rtHz audio-optimised sibling, marketed by LT as an ultralow-noise, low-distortion audio op amp.
LT1128 (same datasheet): use it where unity-gain stability is needed (buffers, some I/V stages).
OPA1611 / OPA211 (TI): about 1.1 nV/rtHz bipolar, unity-gain stable, modern supply range. OPA1612 is the dual.
LME49990 (National/TI, discontinued): 0.9 nV/rtHz, positioned by Aurorasound as a challenger to the LT1028A.
ADA4898-1/-2 (ADI): 0.9 nV/rtHz, unity-gain stable, dual available. Much lower open-loop gain (about 0.14 V/uV) than the LT1028.
open_questions: Web research this run was limited to 6 WebSearch calls. No datasheet revision after Rev D (1028fd, 10/15) and no PCN or die change surfaced. This is a search negative, not proof; the ADI product page's 'Documentation > PCN' section was not read.

Lifecycle: only LT1028ACN8#PBF has web evidence (Octopart 'Production', DigiKey 894417). One search summary claimed an RS Components listing shows it discontinued; that is unconfirmed. Statuses of LT1028CN8/CS8, LT1128ACN8/CN8/CS8 and whether LT1028CSW is now formally obsolete at ADI remain unverified.

Which revision do the older mirrors hold? Candidates: the alldatasheet 70264 LINER copy (20 pages, probably pre-Rev B), Marutsu LT1028.pdf, datasheetcatalog.com, digchip 262 vs 2/041, studylib, manuals.plus and radiolocman. Checking their footers ('1028f', '1028fa', 'LT/TP ...' print codes) would date the original and Rev A sheets.
The Rev A and original datasheets (1028fa / pre-A, and any LT1028-only sheet predating the 1992 combined sheet) remain undated and their contents unknown.
The cds.linear.com/docs/... and linear.com/docs/Datasheet/... seeds are inferred from Linear's naming pattern and were not seen for this part.
Did Texas Instruments second-source the LT1028? The TI macromodel (TEXAS.LIB, 08/31/89) hints at it, but a targeted web search found no TI datasheet or SLOS number.

Community reputation items not re-verified in this run: the Xonar ST/STX I/V popularity (hifivision), the Japanese Dr.DAC impressions (kakaku, jimdofree, otomatsu), Aurorasound's LME49990 positioning, and whether the 'only real L.T. star' post is on page 10 or page 41 of the diyAudio thread (web search surfaced page 41).
Introduction year and designer (commonly attributed to George Erdi, mid-1980s) were not verified. The LT1028 existed by August 1989.

revision_chain_notes:
I found no new vendor, second source or TI literature number. Only the originator's document chain exists: Linear Technology '1028f' followed by the Analog Devices re-host of the same file. The chain from oldest to newest:

(1) Original 1028f edition, (c) 1992 on the combined LT1028/LT1128 sheet. No footer, date or verified copy was found. The single LT1028 sheet from before 1992, before LT1128 was added, is also missing.

(2) Rev A, 1028fa. This is newly evidenced: a search summary quoted the footer '1028fa LT/CP 0901 1.5K REV A • PRINTED IN USA', which reads as September 2001. The copy holding it is not definitively identified. The likeliest is https://www.farnell.com/datasheets/25064.pdf (old Linear typeface); others are radiolocman di=338659, datasheetq and datasheetbank.

(3) Rev B, 1028fb, 10/12. Still no URL of a copy found; searching '1028fb' returned only 1028fd and generic mirrors.

(4) Rev C, 1028fc, 10/14. Held on Scribd, already known.

(5) Rev D, 1028fd, 10/15. Current, hosted by ADI.

Still missing:
- A verified copy of the original (pre-A) edition and its date. The 20-page alldatasheet 70264/70283/70289 copies may be this edition or Rev A.
- The footer date of the pre-1992 single-part LT1028 sheet.
- Any copy of Rev B (1028fb).
- Confirmation of which mirror holds Rev A.

The archive seeds are Linear's legacy URL patterns: cds.linear.com/docs/Datasheet/ before about 2012, and cds.linear.com/docs/en/datasheet/ after. They are derived from those patterns, not seen in the search results, so check them in the Wayback Machine. The www.linear.com/LT1028 form is confirmed by the Rev D page header. The TI second-source question is still unconfirmed; none of the searches found a TI LT1028 datasheet.
